status.en: 342 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 30% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 342 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 30 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Manipur seized a Kuki-Zo camp, took over the Sinai camp, arrested 17 suspects for impersonating SoO cadres and confiscated a large arms cache, while protests erupted over the killing of three Meitei men and police seized 24 firearms. In Kashmir, the IGP called for action against overground workers and hybrid terrorists, reviewed crime disposal and winter preparedness, and warned that police nakas must become more intelligence driven. The BJP rebuked Farooq Abdullah over his statements on PoK, and the VHP joined the attack on his remarks, while the Manipur chief minister proposed a state-wide committee after a query from the prime minister. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Manipur tok kontroll over en Kuki-Zo-leir, overtok Sinai-leiren, arresterte 17 mistenkte for å ha utgitt seg for SoO-kader og konfiskerte en stor våpenbeholdning, mens protester brøt ut etter drapet på tre Meitei-menn og politiet beslagla 24 skytevåpen. I Kashmir oppfordret IGP til tiltak mot overgrunnsarbeidere og hybride terrorister, gjennomgikk kriminalitetsbehandling og vinterberedskap, og advarte om at politiets nakas må bli mer etterretningsdrevet. BJP kritiserte Farooq Abdullah for hans uttalelser om PoK, og VHP sluttet seg til angrepet på hans bemerkninger, mens Manipur-statsministeren foreslo en statlig komité etter en henvendelse fra statsministeren. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
